children.name: Opisthosoma not petiolate, but broadly joined to prosoma (Figures 5-15 through 5-22) Acari (Order: Acari)
Opisthosoma petiolate (Figures 5-5 and 5-9 through 5-13) Araneae (Order: Araneae)

Eyes lacking; tail short, one- to four-segmented; pedipalps arching upward, forward, and downward and moving vertically; body yellowish or brownish, less than 8 mm in length Schizomida (Order: Schizomida)

With two median eyes on a tubercle anteriorly and a group of three eyes on each lateral margin; tail long, filiform, and many-segmented; pedipalps nearly straight or curved mesad, extending forward, and moving laterally (Figure 5-4B); body blackish, more than 50 mm in length Uropygi (Order: Uropygi)
Pedipalps usually much stouter than any of the legs (Figure 5-4B); mostly larger forms
Pedipalps slender, similar to legs (Figure 5-4A); minute forms, 5 mm or less in length Palpigradi (Order: Palpigradi)
Opisthosoma not ending in a sting; first pair of legs longer than other pairs (Figure 5-4A,B); second ventral segment of opisthosoma without comblike organs
Opisthosoma ending in a sting (Figure 5-3); first pair of legs not greatly elongated; second ventral segment of opisthosoma with a pair of comblike organs Scorpiones (Order: Scorpiones)
Prosoma wider than long, lateral margins rounded or arched, and without a transverse suture; opisthosoma without a terminal appendage; length variable, up to about 50 mm Amblypygi (Order: Amblypygi)

Prosoma longer than wide, lateral margins nearly parallel, and with a transverse membranous suture in caudal third; opisthosoma with a very short terminal appendage; length 5-8 mm (see also couplet 6') Schizomida (Order: Schizomida)

Size and color variable, but without broad flap at anterior end of prosoma covering chelicerae; legs variable in length, often very long and slender (Figure 5-14); widely distributed Opiliones (Order: Opiliones)

Orange-red to brown arachnids, about 3 mm in length, with broad flap at anterior end of prosoma concealing chelicerae; legs not unusually long, animal somewhat mitelike or ticklike in appearance; recorded from Rio Grande Valley of Texas Ricinulei (Order: Ricinulei)
First legs similar to the others and (except in the Opiliones) not usually long; opisthosoma not particularly constricted at base
First pair of legs very long, with long tarsi; opisthosoma constricted at base; mainly tropical
Without the preceding combination of characters

Chelicerae very large, usually about as long as prosoma, and extending forward, and body slightly narrowed in middle (Figure 5-4C); color pale yellow to brownish; length 20 to 30 mm; mostly nocturnal desert forms occurring in western United States Solifugae (Order: Solifugae)
Pedipalps raptorial or leglike, but not chelate; body not particularly flattened; size variable
Pedipalps chelate (pincerlike) (Figure 5-23); body more or less oval, flattened, usually less than 5 mm in length Pseudoscorpiones (Order: Pseudoscorpiones)
Opisthosoma without a tail-like prolongation or with a very short leaflike appendage
Opisthosoma with a tail-like prolongation that is either thick and terminating in a sting (Figure 5-3) or slender and more or less whiplike (Figure 5-4A,B); mostly tropical
Opisthosoma distinctly segmented, without spinnerets
Opisthosoma (abdomen) unsegmented or, if segmented, with spinnerets posteriorly on ventral side (Figures 5-5 and 5-8, ALS,PLS,PMS)
